doc.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018

title: Stravinsky, new music and African influence on composition
summary: Rowe links the trio to The Rite of Spring; Daley compares Stravinsky's structure and sources to improvisation, and values screams and colors.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Because I just had the wonderful opportunity to hear “The Rite of Spring” performed live, and I was thinking after I left last night that that came to mind. Because some of the stuff you did almost reminded me of parts of that piece, and I could envision Stravinsky writing all that complex music. You guys achieved the same feel with three people being spontaneous.

Exactly. See that’s the thing. I mean that’s the thing about the whole new music, what they call the new music classical scene, you know. What happens is that for some strange reason, you know, like people like to divide people and put them in boxes and everything. No. If you go to a new music concert of ensemble concerts, you’ll probably hear a lot of the things that we played, most definitely, yeah. But you know so if you go to a new music ensemble concert you’ll hear a lot of the elements that we play on everything. But since we’re improvising it, sometimes, the new music people sometimes look down, you guys are improvising it. Even though we’re getting the same colors and textures and everything. Well the thing about “The Rite of Spring” that was interesting, of course you know they rioted after the concert, I think it was in Paris and everything. They tore the place down. It was like a blast from them — but what Stravinsky was, he tapped into African music, African rhythms and stuff, you know, those polyphonic rhythms. He tapped into it big time. Just like Picasso did he when got into the cubist movement and everything. He tapped into African art and everything. So he tapped into that, for the rhythmic structure of it all and everything. But what I was talking about is that when Stravinsky began to write the piece he had no idea where it would end. It’s the same thing with the improvisation that we’re talking about with Sam. When we start we have no idea where it’s going to end. But when Stravinsky ends the piece then he looks back, he sees the structure of how many movements and stuff, and what this movement does and how this movement — it’s the same thing with Sam. He starts off and he structures us and guides us through and then when we get to the end we look back and we see the structure, we see how we change keys, how we modulated, how we changed tempos, how we changed moods, how we changed textures, you know from going from the piano to the saxophone to the flute, and everything, a lot of the elements that I use in here, using different textures and colors and everything, and moving tempos along and moving textures and colors and yelling. The whole thing is what happens with a lot of musicians when they play, you know, they play but they never put an exclamation point on anything

that they’re doing. Everything is just smooth and beautiful [scats]. And I mean it’s beautiful and technically proficient but sometimes you got to yell out and scream you know. You just can’t be talking in a conversational mode, even though it might be intellectually stimulating and beautiful and amazing technique and everything. Because sometimes you need to yell out and just go, “I need to scream.” And that’s what happens. You saw that with Scott. I mean Scott just, I mean you know how proficient and he can play — but sometimes he just wants to scream and he just screams in the saxophone and he just — and I think those things, because one woman said that she heard the music here last night. She said she heard the music, it just came up into her just like this you know. And it really affected her here. It wasn’t here. She just felt the music right here. So sometimes you need to feel music in different places and everything. So those are important concepts that need to be addressed you know.
